title: The Hessdalen Lights
hook: For decades, mysterious lights have flickered over a remote Norwegian valley.

beats.label: THE CASE
beats.line: In Hessdalen valley, glowing orbs of light drift silently above the mountains.

beats.label: CLUE 1
beats.line: Locals reported seeing the lights as early as the nineteen thirties.

beats.label: CLUE 2
beats.line: Sightings peaked in the early eighties, with up to twenty reports every week.

beats.label: CLUE 3
beats.line: Since 1998, scientists have run automated cameras and sensors at the site.

beats.label: THEORY
beats.line: One theory blames ionized dust or a rare piezoelectric effect from local rock.

beats.label: THE TWIST
beats.line: Even with cameras running, nobody has fully explained what these lights really are.

end.line: What do you think causes the Hessdalen lights?

description: Since the 1930s, strange glowing lights have appeared over Norway's Hessdalen valley, peaking in the early 1980s. Scientists still record them, but no explanation is fully confirmed.

facts.claim: The Hessdalen valley in central Norway has reported unexplained lights since at least the 1930s to 1940s.
Sightings peaked between 1981 and 1984, with reports of up to about 20 lights per week at times.
Project Hessdalen, an automated monitoring station, has recorded the phenomenon since 1998.
Researchers proposed the lights may result from ionized dust or a piezoelectric effect caused by local mineral-rich rock.
No single explanation has been confirmed for all recorded sightings.
The lights are still occasionally recorded by the monitoring station today.
